purpose: Represent a second, analytically distinct proof of the same infinitude-of-primes proposition and compare proof dependency paths.
limits: The proof is represented from modern lecture-note presentations of Euler's argument. Historical attribution to Euler is source-attributed; no claim is made that this record reproduces Euler's original text verbatim. Independent mathematician review remains pending.

nodes.name: Euler product formula for the zeta function
nodes.content: For real s > 1, ζ(s) equals the product over primes p of (1 - p^(-s))^(-1).

nodes.name: Zeta is unbounded as s approaches 1 from above
nodes.content: As real s approaches 1 from above, ζ(s) becomes unbounded.

nodes.name: Euler-style analytic proof of infinitely many primes

sources.author: K. Soundararajan
sources.edition: Lecture notes, Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions, I
sources.locator: Page 1, lines introducing Euler's proof; proof continues through Corollary 2 on page 3
sources.inspection: The notes explicitly recall Euler's proof: ζ(s) has an Euler product for s>1; finitely many primes would keep that product bounded as s→1+, while the zeta sum is unbounded by harmonic-series divergence. The notes further derive divergence of the reciprocal-prime sum.

sources.author: Peter Woit
sources.locator: Section 6.6, Euler product formula and infinitude-of-primes application
sources.inspection: The notes derive the Euler product from unique factorization and explain that ζ(s) tends to infinity as s→1+, which forces infinitely many prime factors in the product.

assumptions_or_framework: real parameter s > 1 for the Euler product identity
standard real-analysis limit as s approaches 1 from above
proofs.method: If there were only finitely many primes, the finite Euler product would remain bounded as s→1+. But ζ(s) is unbounded in that limit, so the prime set cannot be finite.

qualifiers.scope: modern analytic presentation of Euler-style argument

attestations.locator: Page 1: zeta Euler product for s>1
Pages 1–2: ζ(s) unbounded as s→1+ via harmonic-series/integral estimate

proofs.conceptual_route: finite assigned primes → common multiple + 1 → new prime
zeta Euler product + divergence at 1 → finitely many primes impossible

proof_comparison.note: The two records establish the same named proposition through materially different mathematical dependencies. They are not merged, ranked, or treated as separate propositions.

cross_source_check.caveat: Agreement between lecture-note sources is supporting documentation, not independent proof verification.
